newsitem.title: USA: More indictments possible in Texaco case.
newsitem.headline: More indictments possible in Texaco case.

text.p: A federal prosecutor said Wednesday that more defendants could be charged in the Texaco Inc. case involving destruction of documents.
During a hearing in White Plains federal court Assistant U.S. Attorney Stanley Okula told the court that there is a "strong possibility" that additional defendants will be named in a new indictment.

So far, only one former Texaco executive, Richard Lundwall, has been indicted for obstruction of justice. During Wednesday's scheduling hearing in the Lundwall case, Okula asked for additional time to obtain documents that might be used to bring additional charges.

Lundwall, the former senior coordinator of personnel services of Texaco's finance department, was indicted March 13 for obstructing justice in a private race discrimination lawsuit filed against Texaco. He has pleaded not guilty to that charge.
Lundwall was indicted after plea negotiations collapsed with federal prosecutors.

Lundwall had made secret tapes of he and other Texaco executives discussing the destruction of documents requested in the discrimination lawsuit. A Federal Bureau of Investigation agent's affidavit, which is included in court records, said that he had listened to the tapes and had heard other Texaco executives, including the company's former treasurer, discussing how to destroy the documents.
Texaco's treasurer at the time was Robert Ulrich. Ulrich, who has since retired from Texaco, has not been charged by the government.
Lundwall was the lowest level executive at the meetings that were taped.

Okula told U.S. District Judge Barrington Parker he needed additional time to try to obtain documents that were withheld as part of Lundwall's alleged obstructive behaviour. The judge set the next hearing for April 30.
Texaco agreed to settle the race discrimination suit by paying a record $176.1 million. The settlement was approved last month by a federal judge.
